looks_like_me_why: Clear resemblance: same haircut, glasses, skin tone and general face shape are preserved across pages. But it's a strongly stylized CGI/animation interpretation — smoother skin, slightly larger eyes and softer jawline — so it's recognizably me to people who already know me, not 'anyone would recognize me.' A few close-ups (notably pages 9 and 10 while climbing) push the cartoon proportions more than the full-body shots (pages 1–4). Glasses reflections and lens thickness vary slightly between images.
rings_true_why: Narrative is faithful and condensed — all the key beats of Jack and the Beanstalk are present in clear, child-friendly lines. Language and pacing feel like an actual children's picture book. A couple of small departures (the beans look very candy-like; the giant's wife is framed as a 'giant woman' who openly helps) are stylistic, not structural problems.
professional_why: High-quality, consistent art direction: good color grading, coherent lighting, depth-of-field and composition across pages. Typography and image/text pairing are readable and child-appropriate. Small issues keep it from a perfect 'published book' score: minor inconsistencies in facial rendering across some close-ups, a few cartoonish visual cues (e.g. 'Zzz' over the giant) that clash with the otherwise cinematic style, and one odd detail (beans look like brightly colored candy).
not_good: Page 6: the five 'magic beans' look like jellybeans — feels too candy-like for the scene. Pages 9–10 (beanstalk close-ups): facial proportions are noticeably more cartoonish (bigger eyes, softer jaw) compared with the earlier full-body shots. Page 13 (sleeping giant) uses 'Zzz' glyphs which are inconsistent with the otherwise filmic visual style. Minor: glasses reflections/thickness vary between images, and the uploaded photo is not used literally — it's an AI-stylized likeness rather than a faithful photoreal portrait.
liked: Very consistent overall art direction, good composition and color. Illustrations are expressive and convey the story beats clearly. Text is short and well-paced for young readers. Technical polish — lighting, shadows and depth — is strong; the book feels ready to print with only small tweaks needed.
